After Hours: Powerhouse Arts 2026 Staff Art Show (through Dec 6)
events.desc: Exhibitions. Nov 5 to Dec 6. Presented in dialogue with Masterpieces: A Virtual Experience of the Museo del Prado , the Staff Art Show will showcase a range of artistic practices while exploring the broader ecosystem of influence within the arts. Each participating artist will identify an artwork from art history that has shaped their practice, revealing networks of inspiration that connect artists across generations and offering a glimpse into the creative lives of the people who make Powerhouse Arts run.

events.label: Ripple & Rip: Marbling & Collage with Nazli Efe (through Nov 8)
events.desc: Classes & workshops. Nov 7 to Nov 8. In two sessions, experiment with the traditional art of marbling and then create expressive collages using the marbled designs.

events.label: Gold Leaf (through Nov 8)
events.desc: Classes & workshops. Nov 7 to Nov 8. Gilding for printmakers is a custom designed intensive weekend workshop for experienced printmakers who want to use genuine gold and silver leaf in the printing process. The class will focus on two phases: pre-printing and post printing. We will use genuine leaf, metal leaf mica, and metallic powders.

events.label: Anchoring Sight: Figure Drawing with Kiara Ocasio
events.desc: Classes & workshops. Strengthen the connection between observation and gesture in live model figure drawing, through this session led and supported by an instructor.

events.label: Screen Printing: Cards & Stationery (through Nov 22)
events.desc: Classes & workshops. Nov 8 to Nov 22. This 3 week class at MGC Community Print Studio will introduce students to all the skills needed to screen print cards and stationery. Step-by-step instruction, demonstration, and guidance will result in a limited edition on paper. Class goal: 20 1-color cards or equivalent self-directed project.

events.label: Morning Dew: Cyanotypes and Natural Toners with Mickey Aloisio (through Nov 15)
events.desc: Classes & workshops. Nov 14 to Nov 15. Explore the rich possibilities of cyanotypes,as well as alternative photographic printing using organic materials such asgreen tea, coffee, and wine.

events.label: Crafternoons: Crafting a Miniature Museum
events.desc: Classes & workshops. Inspired by the immersive virtual reality exhibition Masterpieces: A Virtual Experience of the Museo del Prado , we’ll paint and sculpt small-scale artworks to fill our museum diorama. Part of our series of free, drop-in art workshops for families, kids, and neighbors of all ages.

events.label: PHA Store pop-up: Al Held Foundation in collaboration with PHA
events.desc: Fairs. Please join us to celebrate Al Held Foundation's first ever posthumous re-issuance of a ceramic object originally created by Al Held. To make this experience available to as many people as possible, all Bargemusic Concerts are Admission Free. Check the Bargemusic website for details on the performance scheduled for each day. Bargemusic concerts are 1 to 1.5 hours, with no intermission. Doors open 20 minutes before the concert (no tickets, no reservations). No food or drink

events.label: Nature Storytime
events.desc: Join for Nature Storytime at the Environmental Education Center! Held at 3:00 PM on the third Thursday of every month (during Open Hours ). Librarians from Brooklyn Public Library Adams Street location lead for an exciting and engaging storytime session, along with singing and rhymes. Each month they select a book to pair with the Education Center’s monthly nature theme. Stick around after to check out all the animals and activities in the room during Open Hours! Storytime is typically about a half hour long.

events.label: Open Hours at the Environmental Education Center (Weekends)
events.desc: Explore Brooklyn Bridge Park like never before during open hours at the Environmental Education Center. The Environmental Education Center is open for free, drop-in hours at 99 Plymouth Street in Dumbo, Brooklyn! Get to know Brooklyn Bridge Park with monthly educational themes, a 250 gallon aquarium filled with critters from the East River, a 10’ scale model of Brooklyn Bridge Park, crafts, a reading corner, and much more. Open Hours offer the opportunity for self-led investigation with guidance by expert educators to reveal the hidden stories found within and around Brooklyn Bridge Park. Don’

events.label: Fall 2026 Jazz Jam
events.desc: 6:00 PM to 10:30 PM. Friday, November 13th • 6-8 PM (Grades 6-12) • 8:30-10:30 PM (Adults) • BKCM Concert Hall (58 7th Avenue) You’re invited to join the students and core faculty of the BKCM Jazz programs for our fall 2026 Jazz Jam! This wonderful annual event is open to all students in our jazz programs to music-make together in […]

events.label: Studio Collective Song Share
events.desc: 7:00 PM to 9:00 PM. Join Studio Collective members in The Joel Foundation Concert Hall to play a song, get feedback and build musical community over snacks and drinks.

events.label: Ziggy and Miles: Presented by the Suzuki Guitar Program
events.desc: 6:00 PM to 7:45 PM. Hailed by The Age as “Australian guitarist brothers making history”, Ziggy and Miles are two of their home country’s finest young musicians forging an international career. BKCM’s Suzuki Guitar Program is thrilled to be hosting the acclaimed duo for a special concert at Grace-Hanson United Methodist Church, just across the street from BKCM Seventh Avenue.

events.label: BCCO Family Concert: Petra and Wolfie
events.desc: 1:00 PM to 4:30 PM. The BCCO’s wild and wacky, Prokofiev-inspired family musical, Petra and Wolfie, returns to the Brooklyn Museum on November 21st.

events.label: Boo!KCM: Live Music & Trick-or-Treating
events.desc: 4:00 PM to 6:00 PM. BKCM’s free, family-friendly Halloween garden party in Park Slope is back! Some have speculated that our 144-year-old Victorian mansion may be haunted. We can neither confirm nor deny these rumors, but we CAN confirm that some talented musical spirits will be giving a spine-chilling performance in the garden, and that the candy will be plentiful and frightfully delicious.

events.label: BCCO Family Concert: Petra and Wolfie – 1 PM Show
events.desc: 1:00 PM to 2:00 PM. The BCCO’s wild and wacky, Prokofiev-inspired family musical, Petra and Wolfie, returns to the Brooklyn Museum on November 21st.

events.label: BCCO Family Concert: Petra and Wolfie – 3:30 PM Show
events.desc: 3:30 PM to 4:30 PM. The BCCO’s wild and wacky, Prokofiev-inspired family musical, Petra and Wolfie, returns to the Brooklyn Museum on November 21st.

events.label: Music Therapy Presents: Sound Bath with Bella Carlucci
events.desc: 7:00 PM to 8:30 PM. Presented by BKCM Music Therapy in the new Joel Foundation Concert Hall, the Sound Bath is a 90-minute immersive and restorative experience led by Bella Carlucci.

events.label: That Feeling In Your Gut: Is This the Right School?
events.desc: 6:30 PM to 8:30 PM. In this webinar, Sarah Birnbaum of New York Special Needs Support will be joined by attorney Greg Cangiano of Skyer Law and neuropsychologists Dr. Laura Tagliareni and Dr. David Salsberg of PALS. Together, we will lay out concrete steps to take, giving you the tools to understand your child’s needs, advocate for them effectively, and set them up for success.

events.label: House Party 2026
events.desc: 7:00 PM to 11:00 PM. Mark your calendars: the Brooklyn Conservatory of Music’s annual House Party returns on November 5, 2026.

events.label: Urban Meadow Halloween Party & Parade
events.location: Mother Cabrini Park and Playground, President Street and Van Brunt Street, Brooklyn, NY, 11231
events.desc: The Urban Meadow Community Garden’s annual Halloween Parade. Get out your costumes: the Underground Horns brass band leads a procession through the neighborhood at noon. events.label: FREE Halloween Walk-Up Paddling – 2nd St.
events.desc: Hop into a Gowanus Dredgers canoe and paddle at your own pace inside the protected Gowanus Canal. Enjoy discovering the canal’s unique mix of wildlife and urban waterway infrastructure, practice your paddling skills, or take a guided audio tour and learn more about the history, cleanup and revitalization of our favorite urban waterway. We’ll outfit you with a life jacket (which must be worn at all times) and paddle, offer some basic instruction on how to paddle and safety tips on how to use a canoe, and help you set off on your own self-guided journey. Trips may be limited to 20 minutes if there’s a crowd — but usually we just expect you to return to the dock 15 min. prior to closing. Who can participate? Paddling is for everyone! Free walk-up canoeing is open to all ages. Groups, families, solo paddlers, and intrepid first dates are all welcome! Minors require a guardian’s signature to participate, and all participants must sign a waiver. What should I wear? Dress for the weather: wear sunscreen, hats, and bring a water bottle — and bring layers if there’s a breeze! Close-toed shoes are recommended, and wear clothing you don’t mind potentially being splashed. Is it really free? Yes! But donations are encouraged to help us continue offering these and other programs. Can I volunteer? Yes! You can sign up to volunteer here. No prior experience is required, but we love return volunteers! Note: Volunteer shifts run from 30-minutes before the start of the program through the first two hours, or from the middle of the program to 30 minutes after the end of the scheduled time.

events.label: Brooklyn Folk Festival: Banjo Toss Competition
events.location: Gowanus Dredgers Canoe Club Boathouse, 165 2nd St, Brooklyn, NY, 11231, United States
events.desc: Each year, as part of the Brooklyn Folk Festival , contestants gather on the banks of the fetid Gowanus Canal to see who can throw a banjo the farthest in the – BANJO TOSS: BANJO THROWING COMPETITION! The special “throwing banjo”, attached to a rope is tossed into the canal, a federally designate Super Fund site. The marked rope pays out, showing how far the banjo has been tossed. It is then hauled back in for the next throw. The Brooklyn Folk Festival is presented each year by the Jalopy Theatre & School of Music, a grassroots Red Hook, Brooklyn community space that is a music venue, music school, and record label. We are excited to support the Banjo Toss event activity so please stop by and join the fun! We are told the best preparation for this competition is to attend a show at the Brooklyn Folk Festival so purchase tickets now before they are sold out. While bearded men and women are growing in popularity as more people live, work and play in our Gowanus neighborhood, we are assured by the organizers that beards are optional. Our amazing collection of competitors reinforces the Dredgers theme of inclusion so stop by to cheer our competitors or compete in the toss as well!

events.label: Creepy Crawly Halloween
events.desc: Take a second look at the creatures that give you the creeps, you may find you like them! Participate in fun activities and experiments that will make your spine tingle at Prospect Park Alliance’s Creepy Crawly Halloween. Nature Detective, 10 am–4 pm What creepy, crawly and curious creatures are hiding in Prospect Park? Borrow a sketchbook and observation guide, then explore indoors and outdoors for spiders, bats, insects, plants, and other wild discoveries. Look closely, sketch what you find, and uncover the mysteries of nature hiding all around you. Owl Pellet Dissection, 11 am–2pm Participants will have the opportunity to pick apart owl pellets, masses of undigested parts of food that owl species occasionally regurgitate! Nature Chef’s Surprise!, 12–3 pm Our nature chef has some tasty treats for you to try that are delicious, nutritious, and crunchy! Take a nibble and earn a special certificate and boasting button. Learn how this mystery treat is a sustainable alternative protein source that has nutritional benefits. events.label: Introduction to Birdwatching Outings
events.desc: Whether you’re new to birding or looking to build your skills, this introductory outing is a great way to explore Prospect Park and learn about the birds that visit throughout the year. Join a member of the Brooklyn Bird Club to learn birding basics and search for the dozens of species found in the park across all seasons. All ages and experience levels are welcome. No registration is required. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. What to Bring: Binoculars if you have them, comfortable walking shoes, water, and weather-appropriate clothing. A limited number of binoculars will be available to borrow. Please Note : Pets are not permitted on this outing. Depending on attendance, participants may be divided into smaller groups. Outings are held rain or shine unless severe weather makes conditions unsafe. Route Description: This outing moves at a relaxed pace with frequent stops to observe birds. Routes may vary from week to week depending on bird activity and park conditions. Participants can expect paved paths, dirt trails, grassy areas, slight inclines and occasional steps. The group will cover approximately 1.5–2 miles. Learn more on the Brooklyn Bird Club website.

events.label: Exhibit: The Shirley Chisholm Way: Brooklyn’s Blueprint for Change
events.desc: Join Prospect Park Alliance and Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute (SCCI) for a new exhibit that explores how Brooklyn’s beloved daughter broke down gender and racial barriers to fight for her community, becoming the first Black woman elected to Congress. The exhibit is organized around seven life lessons drawn from Chisholm’s tenacious career. It features stunning portraits of Chisholm by artist Al Johnson and rarely seen photographs and memorabilia from the Congresswoman’s campaigns, curated by Barbara Bullard, Creative Producer and President of SCCI. These materials offer inspirational insights into how Brooklyn’s beloved daughter broke down gender and racial barriers to become the first Black woman to serve in Congress. This exhibit provides visitors with a space to reflect on Chisholm’s legacy as Prospect Park Alliance welcomes the installation of a new monument in her honor at the Parkside and Ocean Avenue entrance in 2027. The exhibit, curated by Barbara Bullard, Cultural Producer and President of the Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute, is part of Prospect Park Alliance’s ReImagine Lefferts initiative, which is transforming the museum to explore the legacies of resistance and resilience of the Indigenous people of Lenapehoking, whose unceded ancestral lands the park and house rests upon, and Africans who were enslaved by the Lefferts family. The Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute (SCCI) has been at the forefront of art, culture, and justice and economic sustainability since 1977, with the official permission and participation of Congresswoman Chisholm herself in its inception and development. Its purpose is to preserve the legacy of Congresswoman Shirley Chisholm through the initiatives cultivated during her public service career with 21st century activism and innovation. SCCI is aligned with grassroots groups and frontline communities through creating substantive community-based partnership and collaboration along with strategic interoperative relationships with leaders of governmental, and mainstream organizations.

events.label: Brooklyn FAM 6th Annual Flagship Festival: Shine Your Light
events.desc: Brooklyn FAM’s flagship festival is back for its 6th year! Presented in partnership with the Prospect Park Alliance, this year’s free, family-friendly event celebrates our North, Central, and South American indigenous voices, including Nanticoke Lenni-Lenape, Shinnecock, Diné (Navajo), Taíno, Colombian, Mexican, and Guatemalan (Maya). Experience live music and dance performances, workshops, a community drumming circle, craft-making, and public art installations for all ages. Food & beverages will be available for purchase. This event is presented in partnership with the Prospect Park Alliance, American Indian Community House, and New York Immigration Coalition. RSVP About Brooklyn FAM: Brooklyn FAM is a community-empowering, community-building 501(c)3 charitable arts nonprofit. Its mission is to foster cross-community, intergenerational connection, understanding, and empathy for a more just, resilient world. Brooklyn FAM’s vision is a world where difference draws us towards one another. Learn more at brooklynfam.org.

events.label: Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit
events.desc: Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.   Events are subject to change, please check the NYP website for up-to-date information .

events.label: Election Day School Holiday in Prospect Park
events.desc: Join Prospect Park Alliance for family friendly programming on the school holiday for Election Day! Nature Exploration Prospect Park Audubon Center, Free, 10 am–3 pm Join Prospect Park Alliance for nature education programs at the Prospect Park Audubon Center, the first urban Audubon Center in the nation. Leaf Art, 10 am–3 pm: Let’s have fun exploring the unique features of trees and their uniquely shaped leaves. Let your creativity flourish as you craft art inspired by nature. Leaf Litter, 10 am–3 pm: Ever wondered what’s hiding beneath the leaves on the forest floor? Well, there are seeds, leaves, insects, and much more! Join us for our hands-on leaf litter activity to learn all about it. Fall Leaf Discovery, 2–3 pm Join us as we delve into the wonder of nature! Are you curious about why and when trees shed their leaves? Gain hands-on experience in citizen science as we explore the Prospect Park environment and witness how changing temperatures affect the trees. We will provide you with a guide to help you record your observations. This program leaves the Audubon Center promptly at 2 pm. ReImagine Lefferts Open Hours, 12–4 pm Lefferts Historic House, Free Visit the Lefferts Historic House for family friendly outdoor and indoor exhibits, activities, workshops, and special programs that explore the legacies of resistance and resilience of the Indigenous peoples of Lenapehoking, whose unceded lands the park and house rests upon, and the Africans enslaved by the Lefferts family. Carousel Rides, 12–5 pm Children’s Corner, $3 per ride; $13 for a book of 5 tickets; Unlimited with Prospect Park Alliance Family Supporter membership . Celebrate Election Day with the park’s beloved Carousel. Join the Alliance at the Family Supporter level and your family (up to 4 people) will receive unlimited rides on the Carousel for a full year!

events.label: Introduction to Birdwatching Outings
events.desc: Whether you’re new to birding or looking to build your skills, this introductory outing is a great way to explore Prospect Park and learn about the birds that visit throughout the year. Join a member of the Brooklyn Bird Club to learn birding basics and search for the dozens of species found in the park across all seasons. All ages and experience levels are welcome. No registration is required. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. What to Bring: Binoculars if you have them, comfortable walking shoes, water, and weather-appropriate clothing. A limited number of binoculars will be available to borrow. Please Note : Pets are not permitted on this outing. Depending on attendance, participants may be divided into smaller groups. Outings are held rain or shine unless severe weather makes conditions unsafe. Route Description: This outing moves at a relaxed pace with frequent stops to observe birds. Routes may vary from week to week depending on bird activity and park conditions. Participants can expect paved paths, dirt trails, grassy areas, slight inclines and occasional steps. The group will cover approximately 1.5–2 miles. Learn more on the Brooklyn Bird Club website.

events.label: Exhibit: The Shirley Chisholm Way: Brooklyn’s Blueprint for Change
events.desc: Join Prospect Park Alliance and Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute (SCCI) for a new exhibit that explores how Brooklyn’s beloved daughter broke down gender and racial barriers to fight for her community, becoming the first Black woman elected to Congress. The exhibit is organized around seven life lessons drawn from Chisholm’s tenacious career. It features stunning portraits of Chisholm by artist Al Johnson and rarely seen photographs and memorabilia from the Congresswoman’s campaigns, curated by Barbara Bullard, Creative Producer and President of SCCI. These materials offer inspirational insights into how Brooklyn’s beloved daughter broke down gender and racial barriers to become the first Black woman to serve in Congress. This exhibit provides visitors with a space to reflect on Chisholm’s legacy as Prospect Park Alliance welcomes the installation of a new monument in her honor at the Parkside and Ocean Avenue entrance in 2027. The exhibit, curated by Barbara Bullard, Cultural Producer and President of the Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute, is part of Prospect Park Alliance’s ReImagine Lefferts initiative, which is transforming the museum to explore the legacies of resistance and resilience of the Indigenous people of Lenapehoking, whose unceded ancestral lands the park and house rests upon, and Africans who were enslaved by the Lefferts family. The Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute (SCCI) has been at the forefront of art, culture, and justice and economic sustainability since 1977, with the official permission and participation of Congresswoman Chisholm herself in its inception and development. Its purpose is to preserve the legacy of Congresswoman Shirley Chisholm through the initiatives cultivated during her public service career with 21st century activism and innovation. SCCI is aligned with grassroots groups and frontline communities through creating substantive community-based partnership and collaboration along with strategic interoperative relationships with leaders of governmental, and mainstream organizations.

events.label: Battle of Brooklyn Walking Tour
events.desc: Join Flatbush Library and Prospect Park Alliance for a free tour of the park to learn about the Battle of Brooklyn, the first and largest battle of the American War for Independence. This 90 minute tour begins and ends at Lefferts Historic House and takes visitors to the park’s Battle Pass to see the replica fortifications where, on August 27, 1776, thousands of Pennsylvania and New England soldiers fought their British and Hessian counterparts. Along the way, attendees will learn about the battle and its aftermath from the perspective of the Africans enslaved by the Lefferts family, soldiers who fought in what is now Prospect Park and the overall impact of the conflict on Flatbush and Brooklyn. RSVP Please note this tour includes walking up an incline on both asphalt and mulch pathways. Please dress appropriately. This event is generously funded by the Carnegie Corporation of New York, as part of the Carnegie Libraries 250 initiative.

events.label: Exhibit: The Shirley Chisholm Way: Brooklyn’s Blueprint for Change
events.desc: Join Prospect Park Alliance and Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute (SCCI) for a new exhibit that explores how Brooklyn’s beloved daughter broke down gender and racial barriers to fight for her community, becoming the first Black woman elected to Congress. The exhibit is organized around seven life lessons drawn from Chisholm’s tenacious career. It features stunning portraits of Chisholm by artist Al Johnson and rarely seen photographs and memorabilia from the Congresswoman’s campaigns, curated by Barbara Bullard, Creative Producer and President of SCCI. These materials offer inspirational insights into how Brooklyn’s beloved daughter broke down gender and racial barriers to become the first Black woman to serve in Congress. This exhibit provides visitors with a space to reflect on Chisholm’s legacy as Prospect Park Alliance welcomes the installation of a new monument in her honor at the Parkside and Ocean Avenue entrance in 2027. The exhibit, curated by Barbara Bullard, Cultural Producer and President of the Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute, is part of Prospect Park Alliance’s ReImagine Lefferts initiative, which is transforming the museum to explore the legacies of resistance and resilience of the Indigenous people of Lenapehoking, whose unceded ancestral lands the park and house rests upon, and Africans who were enslaved by the Lefferts family. The Shirley Chisholm Cultural Institute (SCCI) has been at the forefront of art, culture, and justice and economic sustainability since 1977, with the official permission and participation of Congresswoman Chisholm herself in its inception and development. Its purpose is to preserve the legacy of Congresswoman Shirley Chisholm through the initiatives cultivated during her public service career with 21st century activism and innovation. SCCI is aligned with grassroots groups and frontline communities through creating substantive community-based partnership and collaboration along with strategic interoperative relationships with leaders of governmental, and mainstream organizations.

events.label: Urban Park Rangers | Fall Foliage Hike

events.label: Pre-Thanksgiving Birding in Prospect Park
events.desc: Join the Prospect Park Alliance and the Brooklyn Bird Club for a morning bird walk exploring the transition from fall to winter in Prospect Park. As seasonal shifts bring new activity to the park’s woodlands and waterways, we will seek out late-autumn arrivals and cold-weather residents, including finches, chickadees, woodpeckers, nuthatches, brown creepers, wrens, wintering waterfowl, and passing raptors. No registration is required. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. Learn more on the Brooklyn Bird Club website.

events.label: Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit
events.desc: Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.   Events are subject to change, please check the NYP website for up-to-date information .

The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.   Events are subject to change, please check the NYP website for up-to-date information .

events.label: Fall Festival at Lakeside
events.desc: Celebrate the season at the Lakeside Fall Festival, a month-long fall experience filled with pumpkins, Haunted Hotel experience, carnival games, family activities, seasonal treats, photo ops, and Halloween fun in the heart of Prospect Park. Pick a pumpkin, make your way through the corn maze, challenge your family to carnival games, test your skills, grab something seasonal to eat, and spend the day enjoying fall at LeFrak Center at Lakeside. The Fall Festival is designed to be family friendly and fun for all ages. Mondays: Festival 3–6 PM , Haunted Hotel 4–10 PM Thursdays-Fridays: Festival 3–6 PM, Haunted Hotel 6–10 PM Saturdays: Festival 11AM–6 PM, Haunted Hotel 4–11 PM Sundays: Festival 11AM–6 PM, Haunted Hotel 4–10 PM Get Tickets

events.label: FIDO Coffee Bark
events.desc: Coffee Bark is an opportunity for Brooklyn dog owners to chat over coffee and pastries while their dogs romp and play over dog biscuits. With dozens of dogs and people, Coffee Bark is an amazing sight. Look for coffee, pastries, dog biscuits and information about off-leash activities just south of the Picnic House. Hosted by FIDO of Brooklyn , this event is always free! For up to date information about the status of Coffee Bark events in the case of inclement weather, please visit the FIDO in Prospect Park website.

events.label: Introduction to Birdwatching Outings
events.desc: Whether you’re new to birding or looking to build your skills, this introductory outing is a great way to explore Prospect Park and learn about the birds that visit throughout the year. Join a member of the Brooklyn Bird Club to learn birding basics and search for the dozens of species found in the park across all seasons. All ages and experience levels are welcome. No registration is required. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. What to Bring: Binoculars if you have them, comfortable walking shoes, water, and weather-appropriate clothing. A limited number of binoculars will be available to borrow. Please Note : Pets are not permitted on this outing. Depending on attendance, participants may be divided into smaller groups. Outings are held rain or shine unless severe weather makes conditions unsafe. Route Description: This outing moves at a relaxed pace with frequent stops to observe birds. Routes may vary from week to week depending on bird activity and park conditions. Participants can expect paved paths, dirt trails, grassy areas, slight inclines and occasional steps. The group will cover approximately 1.5–2 miles. Learn more on the Brooklyn Bird Club website.

events.label: New Year’s Eve Fireworks in Prospect Park
events.desc: Prospect Park Alliance, the non-profit organization that sustain’s Brooklyn’s flagship park, will present Brooklyn’s most spectacular New Year’s Eve Fireworks celebration at the iconic Grand Army Plaza. RSVP Tickets for this event are recommended but not required and will not be checked at the event.

Established in 1989, the Grand Army Plaza greenmarket is the flagship Brooklyn market. EBT/Food Stamps and WIC & Senior FMNP coupons accepted year-round. Learn More For a full calendar of events and a list of sellers, visit the GrowNYC website. Learn about all Nutrition Benefit Programs accepted at GrowNYC Markets.

events.label: Introduction to Birdwatching Outings
events.desc: Whether you’re new to birding or looking to build your skills, this introductory outing is a great way to explore Prospect Park and learn about the birds that visit throughout the year. Join a member of the Brooklyn Bird Club to learn birding basics and search for the dozens of species found in the park across all seasons. All ages and experience levels are welcome. No registration is required. Children under 12 must be accompanied by an adult. What to Bring: Binoculars if you have them, comfortable walking shoes, water, and weather-appropriate clothing. A limited number of binoculars will be available to borrow. Please Note : Pets are not permitted on this outing. Depending on attendance, participants may be divided into smaller groups. Outings are held rain or shine unless severe weather makes conditions unsafe. Route Description: This outing moves at a relaxed pace with frequent stops to observe birds. Routes may vary from week to week depending on bird activity and park conditions. Participants can expect paved paths, dirt trails, grassy areas, slight inclines and occasional steps. The group will cover approximately 1.5–2 miles. Learn more on the Brooklyn Bird Club website.

events.label: Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit
events.desc: Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.   Events are subject to change, please check the NYP website for up-to-date information .

events.label: Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit
events.desc: Prospect Park Alliance is collaborating with NewYork-Presbyterian to offer comprehensive sexual health services in Brooklyn’s backyard at Grand Army Plaza every Thursday from 10 am to 3 pm and every Monday at the Parkside + Ocean Avenue Entrance from 10 am to 3 pm. The NewYork-Presbyterian Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is a safe, inclusive space for people to receive high-quality sexual health services. Learn more about the Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit in Prospect Park or reach out to us at mobilehealth@nyp.org or (929) 923-3543. No insurance or ID is required to receive care. Staffed by a team of NewYork-Presbyterian healthcare providers, the mobile medical unit has an exam room and consult room, and offers routine laboratory testing, vaccinations, and PrEP and PEP medications that lower the risk of HIV infection. Patients can also be connected to social services, benefits enrollment, and local healthcare providers. Other services include sexually transmitted infection (STI) testing, family planning, hepatitis C screening, health education and more. The Sexual Health Mobile Medical Unit is made possible through funding from the Dalio Center for Health Justice and the Division of Community and Population Health at NewYork-Presbyterian, and a grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention.
